propositions: The reconciler permanently loses candidates it fails to vote by advancing the cursor to newest event in a window regardless of per-candidate outcomes, violating the contract that timeouts and errors are retried next pass.
Gerrit webhook delivery is at-most-once (not at-least-once as documented), so the reconciler is the only recovery path for dropped uploads, making the cursor bug a silent outage.

A non-newest candidate that times out or errors is excluded from all future reconciler windows because the events-log ?t1= filter is server-side, causing indefinite stall until a manual nudge (recheck-review or rebase) mints a new event after the cursor.
The test double records the events-log since parameter but ignores it, so the production cursor filtering behavior is never exercised by existing reconciler tests and the defect shipped undetected.

An agent cannot distinguish between bot-down, review-in-flight, change-queued-behind-N, and change-never-queued because queue depth and per-lane vote attribution are not exposed on /health or in logs.

Terminal outcomes (skipped/post_vote_closed, skipped/dedup, already_voted) must advance the cursor, while retryable outcomes (deferred, error, reconcile_check_error, review_timeout) must be held back until a bounded hold-back ceiling to prevent a chronically-stuck change from pinning the window forever.
